description: Engine API bodies that carry the document format: the session and what the engine supports, the profile list and creating and duplicating profiles, documents, blobs, commits, undo, redo and revert and their results, problems, integration tokens, sensors and their readings, the engine settings, the engine's recent log entries, the displays, and the preview socket's messages, frame headers (with item bounds) and change events. spec/openapi.json says which request carries which. See docs/api.md, docs/commit.md and docs/geometry.md.

session.description: GET /api/session: the engine, this run of it and what it supports.

engineBuild.description: The source revision the engine was built from, for a bug report (docs/api.md#session): the commit's abbreviated id as git writes it, such as "004cf52", followed by "-dirty" when the build had changes not yet committed; "unknown" when the build couldn't tell (built without git or outside a repository, as from a source archive). A client shows it as given.

protocol.description: The engine API's version: 2 for the API these schemas describe. It goes up only when the API changes in a way a client can't ignore (a member or endpoint removed or changed); members and endpoints are added without changing it.

instance.description: This run of the engine: new every time the engine starts, so a client that sees another knows the engine restarted (and that every document tag it read before is stale). Not a document's tag: a commit names its document's (documentResponse).

started.description: When this run of the engine started, in UTC to the second. The same for the whole run, like `instance`.

features.description: The optional API features the engine has, by name, each once (docs/api.md#session): every operation added after this version of the API comes under one, and a client uses it only when its name is listed. This version defines none, so the list is empty. A client ignores a name it doesn't know.

platform.description: The operating system the engine runs on. A client treats a platform it doesn't know as `other`.

osVersion.description: The operating system's version as it reports it, for a bug report: on macOS its product version ("26.1", "15.6.1"), on Windows major.minor.build ("10.0.26100"), on Linux the kernel release ("6.8.0-45-generic"); "unknown" when the engine can't read it. Each system writes its own: a client shows it as given.

arch.description: The processor architecture the engine runs as: the engine's own, so an engine emulated on another architecture reports the one it was built for. A client treats an architecture it doesn't know as `other`.

dataDir.description: The folder the engine keeps its data in: an absolute path on the engine's machine.

mock.description: Whether the engine runs in mock mode, started to simulate its sensors (docs/api.md#session): its readings come from simulated sources, not the computer's, so a client can say they aren't real. It changes only when the engine restarts.

sessionMedia.description: The media the engine can show beyond stored assets (docs/api.md#session): `providers`, the media providers configured on it by name (docs/providers.md), each once. A scene's provider source names one of them; `media.provider` in the scene format's capabilities says only that providers exist. It changes only when the engine restarts.

providers.description: Provider names, as a provider source's `provider` is written (`http`: web images). A client ignores a name it doesn't know.

sessionLocale.description: The PC's regional format as the engine read it when it started (docs/api.md#session): a profile without a `locale` draws numbers and dates with it, and a client that formats readings of its own uses it so they match the frames. It changes only when the engine restarts.

tag.description: Its language and region, such as en-SG; `und` when the engine knows no language for it.

decimalSeparator.description: Written between a number's integer digits and its decimals.

groupSeparator.description: Written between groups of three integer digits.

apiFeature.description: The name of an optional API feature (session.features), written as a capability is: lower-case words joined by dots.

instanceId.description: An opaque id, compared for equality only: a run of the engine (the session's and hello's `instance`), or a document's lifetime tag (a profile entry's, a document response's and a doc event's `instance`, docs/api.md#a-documents-tag), new every time the engine creates or opens the document. A document's revisions belong to its tag.

profileEntry.description: One profile in GET /api/profiles, an array of these in display order, and the 201 answer to creating or duplicating one. `status` says whether the engine can open the profile's document, and which members come with it: ok (name, width, height, rev and dirty), unsupported (it needs a format major version or document capability this engine lacks: a problem, and the name when the document has one) or unreadable (the stored document can't be read, isn't JSON, or breaks the document schema or a document limit outside its scenes: a problem only). Every entry has the document's tag, `instance`, which its DELETE names. An unsupported or unreadable profile is listed and deleted, never opened and never exported (docs/unsupported.md). A client treats a status it doesn't know as a profile it can't open.

profileEntryOk.description: A profile whose document the engine opens. A document with invalid or unsupported scenes is ok: those items are placeholders (docs/unsupported.md).

instance.description: The document's tag: the same as its document response's and doc events'.

dirty.description: The document has changes that aren't saved.

recovered.description: When the document's unsaved changes were kept before the engine last stopped (docs/document.md#revisions): present from the restore until the document is saved or reverted. A client shows it only while `dirty`.

profileEntryUnsupported.description: A profile whose document needs a format major version or a document capability this engine lacks.

instance.description: The profile's tag, new when the engine first reads it in a run: what its DELETE names.

name.description: The document's `profile.name` when that is a string of 1–256 characters, else absent.

problem.description: Why the engine doesn't open it: `unsupported.format` (at /format) or `unsupported.capability` (at /requires/i), with a JSON pointer into the stored document.

profileEntryUnreadable.description: A profile whose stored document can't be read, isn't JSON, or breaks the document schema or a document limit outside its scenes.

instance.description: The profile's tag, new when the engine first reads it in a run: what its DELETE names.

problem.description: The first problem found, with a JSON pointer into the stored document: `io` (the file can't be read), `json` (not JSON) or a document check's code (`schema`, `limit.documentBytes`, ...; docs/validation.md).

profileStatusProblem.description: 409 application/problem+json: the profile's document can't be opened (its status is unsupported or unreadable), so it can't be read, changed, saved, drawn or exported. It can still be listed and deleted.

code.description: The profile's status. A client treats a status it doesn't know as a profile it can't open.

createProfileRequest.description: POST /api/profiles: a new profile under a client-chosen id, either empty (a canvas with no items) or from a document. An id that already exists: 409 existsProblem. Answered 201 with the new profile's profileEntry (docs/api.md).

createProfileEmpty.description: An empty profile: a document with this name and canvas size and no items.

id.description: The new profile's id, chosen by the client.

createProfileFromDocument.description: A profile from a document (importDocument), checked as a stored document is: a scene that is invalid or unsupported (or over a budget) is kept as sent and drawn as a placeholder; a document the engine wouldn't open is refused (422). The document's own `id` (optional; a document id when given) is replaced by `id`, and its `rev` members are ignored.

id.description: The new profile's id, chosen by the client.

importDocument.description: A document (infopanel.document/1) as a create takes it: the document format with its `id` and `rev` members optional (they are ignored: the create's `id` replaces the document's) and every scene taken as stored (storedScene), so a document the engine exported, with scenes it draws as placeholders, can be created again. Its scenes are then checked as a stored document's are (docs/api.md).

items.description: Top-level items in drawing order: the first is at the back.

importSceneItem.description: A scene item as a create takes it (document format: sceneItem), with its scene as stored.

importGroupItem.description: A group item as a create takes it (document format: groupItem).

children.description: In drawing order: the first is at the back.

duplicateProfileRequest.description: POST /api/profiles/{id}/duplicate: a copy of the profile's current document under a client-chosen id. An id that already exists: 409 existsProblem. Answered 201 with the copy's profileEntry.

id.description: The copy's id, chosen by the client.

existsProblem.description: 409 application/problem+json: a profile with the requested id already exists (a create or duplicate whose first attempt succeeded, retried, gets this). Nothing was created.

documentResponse.description: GET /api/profiles/{id}: the profile's current document, with its revision members (the `rev` of the document, the profile and every item), and its state.

instance.description: The document's tag (docs/api.md#a-documents-tag), which these revisions belong to: what its commits, undo, redo, revert and DELETE name, and a save may. Not the session's instance.

rev.description: The document's revision: the same as `document.rev`.

dirty.description: The document differs from the saved one.

recovered.description: When the document's unsaved changes were kept before the engine last stopped (docs/document.md#revisions): present from the restore until the document is saved or reverted. A client shows it only while `dirty`.

responseDocument.description: A document (infopanel.document/1) as the engine returns it: every revision member set, and every scene exactly as stored (storedScene).

items.description: Top-level items in drawing order: the first is at the back.

responseProfile.description: The document's profile, with `rev`: the document revision at which a profile field last changed.

responseSceneItem.description: A scene item as the engine returns it (document format: sceneItem), with its `rev` and its scene as stored.

rev.description: The document revision at which the item last changed.

responseGroupItem.description: A group item as the engine returns it (document format: groupItem), with its `rev`.

rev.description: The document revision at which the item last changed.

children.description: In drawing order: the first is at the back.

storedScene.description: A scene exactly as stored: an object with a string `format`. A scene the engine draws normally matches the scene schema (urn:infopanel:scene:1); one it draws as a placeholder (it needs a newer format or a capability the engine lacks, breaks a rule or limit, or can't be compiled) is returned unchanged and may not (docs/unsupported.md).

blobInfo.description: POST /api/blobs: a stored blob. The engine stores any bytes up to the `videoBytes` limit (more: 413, not stored), named by their SHA-256, and inspects them as a media asset: the answer has `media`, what it found, or `mediaError`, why they can't be used as media (a scene's media naming such a blob draws the missing-media placeholder).

blobInfoMedia.description: A stored blob that is a media asset within the media limits.

id.description: `sha256:` and the SHA-256 of the bytes as sent, in lower-case hex.

bytes.description: The blob's size in bytes: at most `videoBytes` (256 MiB, docs/limits.md); a picture's used as media at most `mediaBytes` (32 MiB).

blobInfoMediaError.description: A stored blob that can't be used as media: not media at all, or media that breaks a media check (a picture over `mediaBytes` included).

id.description: `sha256:` and the SHA-256 of the bytes as sent, in lower-case hex.

bytes.description: The blob's size in bytes: at most `videoBytes` (256 MiB, docs/limits.md); a picture's used as media at most `mediaBytes` (32 MiB).

mediaError.description: Why the bytes can't be used as media: the media check's first error (docs/validation.md: `media.*`, or a `limit.*` code: `limit.mediaBytes` for a picture over 32 MiB, never `limit.videoBytes`, whose bytes aren't stored), with path "".

mediaInfo.description: A media asset as the engine read it from its header or container, without decoding it (docs/validation.md). Sizes are in pixels; an SVG's come from its `width` and `height` or its `viewBox` (docs/svg.md); a video's are its first video track's coded size (docs/smart-nodes.md, video files).

format.description: The asset's format: an image's, or a video's container (`mp4` for mp4 and mov, `matroska` for mkv and webm, `avi`). A client treats a format it doesn't know as it treats the others: media the engine draws.

frames.description: 1 for a still image; an animation's frame count; a video's frame count as its container states it, 1 when it states none.

duration.description: An animation's length in seconds (one loop); 0 for a still image; a video's length as its container states it, 0 when it states none.

codec.description: A video's codec; absent for an image. A client treats a codec it doesn't know as it treats the others: a video the engine plays.

commitRequest.description: POST /api/profiles/{id}/commit. The ops apply in order, all or none, as one undo step (or merged into the previous one, see coalesceKey).

opId.description: Unique per commit, chosen by the client (a UUID, say). Retrying with the same opId and the same body (byte for byte) returns the first result without applying anything again.

instance.description: The tag of the document the client's revisions came from (its documentResponse, profile entry or doc event). Another one (the engine restarted, or the profile was deleted and created again): 409 with reason "instance".

baseRev.description: The document revision the commit is based on: the document `rev` the client last read before it built the commit. It tells a retry from a new commit once the engine has forgotten older opIds: an unknown opId whose baseRev is older than the engine's retry window, or at or below its retry watermark and older than the document's `rev`, is refused (409 expiredProblem; docs/commit.md). Greater than the document's `rev`: 422 (baseRev.future). Each op's own `baseRev` decides its conflicts.

coalesceKey.description: Merge this commit's undo step into the previous one when that had the identical key and the key starts with "gesture:" or less than 1 s passed. A key names one gesture of one client: it includes a random part chosen once per client instance ("gesture:5b0e8f0c-3c1d-4b8e-a7f2-1d9c6e4a2b7f:7").

baseRev.description: The document revision the change is based on: the document `rev` the client last read, for every kind of op (not the item's own `rev`). The op conflicts when a field group it writes (for `remove`, any field of the item or of anything in it) last changed at a revision greater than this. Greater than the document's `rev`: the commit is refused (422, baseRev.future). Absent: no check.

setDesignOp.description: Replaces a scene item's design: layout, source and scene together (absent or null layout or source: none), and its origin when given (null removes it; absent keeps it).

setAttributesOp.description: Sets the given attributes of an item (scene or group); one given as null is removed (docs/commit.md).

insertOp.description: Adds an item (with its children, for a group) to the top level (parentId absent or null) or to a group, at `index` (past the end of the list, or absent: the end, the front).

removeOp.description: Removes an item and everything in it.

moveOp.description: Moves an item to `index` (in the target list once the item has been taken out; past its end: the end) of the top level or a group. Its placement is kept as it is (local coordinates) unless `placement` is given.

itemIndex.description: A position in a list of items, 0 first (at the back). At most 2,000, the document's item limit: a larger value is invalid, never clamped. An index past the end of the list means the end.

opIndex.description: The index of an op in its commit: below 1,000, the op limit.

parentRef.description: A group's item id, or null (or absent) for the top level.

profileOp.description: Sets the given profile fields; each replaces the field whole, and an optional one given as null is removed (docs/commit.md). name, width and height can't be removed.

historyRequest.description: The body of POST /api/profiles/{id}/undo, /redo and /revert, and optionally of /save: the state the client's request is based on. Another document's tag: 409 conflictProblem (reason "instance"); a `baseRev` greater than the document's `rev`: 422 invalidProblem (baseRev.future); a document whose `rev` isn't `baseRev`: 409 conflictProblem (reason "changed"); nothing is done in each case (docs/commit.md).

instance.description: The tag of the document the client's revision came from (its documentResponse, profile entry or doc event).

baseRev.description: The document `rev` the client last read: the request acts only while the document is still at that revision.

commitResult.description: 200 response to a commit, and to undo, redo, revert and save (docs/commit.md).

rev.description: The document's revision after the commit (unchanged when nothing changed).

items.description: The new `rev` of every item the commit (or undo, redo or revert) changed or added.

profileRev.description: The profile's new `rev`, when the commit changed it.

replayed.description: true when this is the stored result of an earlier commit with the same opId.

commitWarning.description: Accepted, but not drawn as written: code "unsupported" (the scene needs a format or capability this engine lacks; it is kept as it is and drawn as a placeholder).

conflictProblem.description: 409 application/problem+json to a commit, undo, redo, revert or save: nothing was applied or saved. The client refetches, rebuilds its change on the current state and sends it again (a commit with a new opId). A DELETE's 409 is deleteConflictProblem.

conflicts.description: A commit's: every conflict found, at least one. An undo's, redo's, revert's or save's: one `instance` conflict, or one `changed` conflict for each item (and for the profile) with a field group changed after its baseRev. That list can be empty: items removed since are not listed, and an undo, redo or revert step may change no field group.

deleteConflictProblem.description: 409 application/problem+json to a DELETE naming another document's tag: nothing was deleted. The client reads the profile again (its entry or its document).

rev.description: The document's current revision. Absent for a profile that can't be opened, which has none.

op.description: The op that conflicts. Absent when the conflict is the whole request's: reason instance, and every conflict of an undo, redo, revert or save.

reason.description: changed: a field group the op writes last changed at a revision greater than the op's baseRev (see `fields`; for `remove`, any field group of the item or of anything in it, each listed with its own `id`); for an undo, redo, revert or save, a field group that changed after its baseRev. missing: the item or parent doesn't exist at that point of the commit. instance: the request names another tag than the document's (the engine restarted, or the profile was deleted and created again, since the client read it). A client treats a reason it doesn't know as it treats every conflict: it refetches and rebuilds its change.

fields.description: The field groups that changed (docs/commit.md): placement, design, bindings, name, visible, locked, position (parent, and index among the siblings present in both versions), children (a group's membership: an item added to it or taken out of it), or a profile field's name.

expiredProblem.description: 409 application/problem+json: the commit's opId isn't one the engine remembers, and its baseRev is older than the engine's retry window, or at or below its retry watermark (the newest baseRev of a forgotten commit) while the document has moved past it, so the engine can't tell whether it is a retry of a commit it applied and has since forgotten. Nothing was applied. The client reads the document, decides whether its change is still needed, and if so commits it again with a new opId and a current baseRev (docs/commit.md).

invalidProblem.description: 422 application/problem+json: the request body (a commit, a create, duplicate, undo, redo, revert or save body, or a document) breaks the format, a rule or a limit; nothing was applied.

errors.description: Every error, at most 100, then, when there were more, one last error with code `more` (path "") counting the rest (docs/validation.md).

path.description: The exact JSON pointer to what the error is about, in what was checked: the request body, or the stored document or blob (docs/versioning.md#error-codes-and-paths).

code.description: A code from docs/limits.md and docs/validation.md (schema, limit.*, ref.*, type.*, ...). A later engine may add codes: a client handles a code it doesn't know by its family, else by the answer's HTTP status (docs/versioning.md#error-codes-and-paths).

message.description: What went wrong, for people: display text, never read by a client.

itemBounds.description: Where an item is drawn this frame, in profile pixels. `frame` is the layout box (automatic dimensions measured), `ink` what the item covers including effects; both are rectangles before rotation, each rotated by `rotation` degrees about its own centre.

problem.description: Set when the item is drawn as a placeholder: unsupported (needs a newer engine), invalid (breaks a rule or limit), budget (over a document or process budget). A client treats a problem it doesn't know as a placeholder whose reason it can't name.

itemMedia.description: Set when media the item shows had a problem in this tick: the first one, as the engine reports it (docs/api.md#frames). The item itself isn't a placeholder: the media is drawn as the missing-media placeholder, or a provider's last good image stays while it says why the newest couldn't be shown.

code.description: `media.loading` (still loading), `media.missing` (an asset that isn't stored, or was refused), `media.provider` (the provider couldn't fetch it, or the reference isn't one it takes), `media.address` (an address the engine may not connect to, docs/providers.md), `media.budget` (a video past the engine's decode sessions, docs/smart-nodes.md), or the code a fetched answer was refused with (docs/validation.md: `media.format`, `limit.mediaBytes`, ...). A client treats a code it doesn't know as media that can't be shown.

message.description: Why, for people, in English, such as "The server answered 404."; one longer than 1,024 characters is cut, ending in "…".

frameHeader.description: The JSON header of a frame message on /ws (docs/api.md): the document revision and tick the frame was drawn from, its encoding, scale and size, and where every item is.

tick.description: The render tick the frame was drawn from (docs/identity.md). Within one subscription, frames with the same tick were drawn from the same tick snapshot, and tick numbers never go down.

frameId.description: The frame's number: unique within one run of the engine, and greater for a frame rendered later.

encoding.description: How the payload after the header is encoded: `png`, the whole frame as a PNG; `h264`, one H.264 access unit of the subscription's video stream (docs/api.md#video-frames). A subscription gets only the encodings it can ask for.

keyframe.description: On an `h264` frame: whether it decodes on its own. A decoder starts, and after a size change starts again, at a keyframe.

codec.description: On an `h264` keyframe: the codec string `avc1.PPCCLL` (profile, constraint flags and level, in hexadecimal, from the stream's SPS) to configure a decoder with.

description.description: On an `h264` keyframe: the decoder configuration record (avcC, ISO/IEC 14496-15) of the stream from this keyframe on, in base64. Its SPS says the stream never reorders frames.

encoder.description: On an `h264` keyframe: whether the stream from it on is encoded in `hardware` or `software`. A client shows a value it doesn't know as it is.

fallback.description: On a `png` frame of an `h264` subscription: why it isn't video. `encoder.unavailable`: the engine has no working H.264 encoder; `encoder.failed`: its encoders failed or are busy during this subscription; `encoder.size`: the frame is larger than the video size, or no encoder takes its size. A client reads a value it doesn't know as "video unavailable for this frame".

encodeMs.description: The milliseconds from handing the frame's pixels to its encoder to having the encoded frame: for `h264`, copying and encoding, waiting for the encoder included; for `png`, that PNG's encoding (one PNG may serve several subscriptions).

skipped.description: The frames the engine drew for this subscription and didn't send since the last one it sent (dropped before encoding, or replaced by a newer one before it could be sent).

scale.description: Frame pixels per profile pixel: 0.1 or a multiple of 0.25 from 0.25 to 4. The subscription's scale rounded to a step of 0.25, then lowered while the frame would be over 16 Mpx (docs/api.md#frames).

pixelWidth.description: The frame's width in pixels: profileWidth × scale, rounded (docs/api.md#frames). pixelWidth × pixelHeight is at most 16,777,216.

pixelHeight.description: The frame's height in pixels: profileHeight × scale, rounded (docs/api.md#frames).

profileWidth.description: The profile's canvas width at `rev`, in profile pixels.

profileHeight.description: The profile's canvas height at `rev`, in profile pixels.

itemBounds.description: The bounds of every visible item that has bounds, from the same tick as the pixels, in document order: a group before its children (docs/geometry.md). Each id appears once.

docEvent.description: The `doc` message on /ws: the subscribed document's state. Sent when the subscription starts and after every change to the document or its state (a commit, undo, redo, revert or save, from any client). The engine keeps only the latest state to send: a client that falls behind gets the newest, so it may skip revisions, and the last one it gets is always current. It carries no content; the document at that revision is read with GET /api/profiles/{id}.

instance.description: The document's tag, which `rev` belongs to (docs/api.md#a-documents-tag).

dirty.description: The document differs from the saved one.

recovered.description: When the document's unsaved changes were kept before the engine last stopped (docs/document.md#revisions): present from the restore until the document is saved or reverted. A client shows it only while `dirty`.

formatSupport.description: What an engine supports (part of GET /api/session), by format string: every format it reads, each with the newest minor version of it the engine reads, the format's optional capabilities the engine has and the format's limits. A client ignores a format string it doesn't know.

formatString.description: A format string: a format's name and its major version, such as `infopanel.scene/1` (docs/versioning.md).

version.description: The newest minor version of the format the engine reads, such as "1.0"; it reads every earlier one of the same major version.

capabilities.description: The format's optional capabilities the engine has (docs/versioning.md#capabilities-and-requires). A client ignores one it doesn't know.

limits.description: The format's limits, by name (docs/limits.md says which format each belongs to). A client ignores a name it doesn't know.

createTokenRequest.description: POST /api/tokens (the session token only): a new integration token with a name and scopes. Answered 201 with createdToken, the only answer that carries the token's secret (docs/api.md#authentication).

scopes.description: What the token may do: `read`, `edit` or both. `edit` implies `read`, and the token is answered and listed with both.

tokenInfo.description: An integration token, without its secret: GET /api/tokens (the session token only) answers an array of these, oldest first. The session token is never listed.

kind.description: The token's kind: `integration`, the only kind the API creates and lists.

scopes.description: What the token may do: always `read`, and `edit` when it may change profiles, documents and blobs.

lastUsed.description: When the token last authenticated a request, kept to within a minute; absent when it never has.

createdToken.description: 201 to POST /api/tokens: the new token's tokenInfo members and its secret, `token`, which no other answer carries and the engine doesn't keep (it stores only a hash).

token.description: The secret, sent as `Authorization: Bearer {token}` or on /ws like the session token: `ipi_` and 43 base64url characters (256 random bits).

tokenId.description: An integration token's id, used to revoke it (DELETE /api/tokens/{id}): 32 lower-case hex digits. Not a secret.

tokenName.description: A token's name, for people: 1 to 64 letters, digits, spaces, dots, underscores and hyphens, without a space at either end.

items.description: A scope (docs/api.md#authentication). In what the engine sends, a client shows a scope it doesn't know by its name.

timestamp.description: A UTC time to the second (RFC 3339), such as "2026-10-27T09:30:00Z".

scopeProblem.description: 403 application/problem+json: the token is valid but lacks the scope the request needs: `read` or `edit`, or `session` for what only the session token may do (signing in, the token endpoints, the engine settings, the recent log entries, opening the engine's folders). A missing, unknown or revoked token is answered 401 instead (docs/api.md#authentication).

scope.description: What the request needs. A client shows a scope it doesn't know by its name: the request is refused all the same.

problem.description: application/problem+json (RFC 9457) for an error without a definition of its own: 400 (a query parameter that isn't a whole number, GET /ws without a WebSocket upgrade), 401 (no valid token), 403 (a request from an origin the engine doesn't accept), 404 (no such profile, blob, token, folder or endpoint), 405, 413 (a blob over mediaBytes) and 500 (an engine error, a folder the engine couldn't open, or displays it couldn't list). Its members are for people; a client acts on the status (docs/api.md#errors).

type.description: A URI for the kind of error: the HTTP status's section of RFC 9110.

title.description: The HTTP status's reason phrase, such as "Not Found".

sensorEntry.description: One sensor in GET /api/sensors, an array of these: a sensor the engine's sources offer, with the `key` a binding names (docs/bindings.md) and its status now.

key.description: The sensor's key, as a binding's `key` names it. Opaque.

source.description: The id of the source that offers the sensor.

group.description: The group the source lists the sensor in (a device, say), for people.

unit.description: The unit of its values, for people ("°C", "%"); empty when it has none.

status.description: `live` (a current reading), `stale` (a reading older than the source normally updates, the last value kept), `unavailable` (no reading), `denied` (the operating system refused the engine access to the sensor), `simulated` (no source handles the key; the engine simulates it, in mock mode only) or `missing` (the key isn't well formed). A scene input bound to the sensor reads it as docs/bindings.md#status maps it. A client treats a status it doesn't know as no reading.

sensorValue.description: One reading in GET /api/sensors/values, an array of these: every listed sensor (sensorEntry) that has a reading now, in list order. A sensor without one is left out.

now.description: The current value (the last one when the reading is stale). A value that isn't a finite number is 0.

min.description: The lowest value the source has reported.

max.description: The highest value the source has reported.

avg.description: The average of the values the source has reported.

unit.description: The unit of its values, for people; empty when it has none.

text.description: A text or table sensor's text ("" for a table without one); absent for a number sensor.

history.description: With `?history=n` (n of 1 or more): a number sensor's last n samples at most, oldest first, one every `graphRate` milliseconds (engineSettings; one a second by default, docs/bindings.md#history). Absent otherwise, and for a text or table sensor.

status.description: `live`, or `stale` for the last value of a sensor that has stopped updating. A client treats a status it doesn't know as no reading.

engineSettings.description: GET /api/settings, and the answer to PATCH /api/settings: the engine settings in effect, each the value set or its default, with how many changes this run made to the stored settings and whether the engine could read them (docs/api.md#settings). `status` tells the two shapes apart: `ok` without a `problem` (engineSettingsOk), or the settings the engine couldn't read with the `problem` (engineSettingsProblem). Read tolerantly: a later engine may add settings, and a client ignores members it doesn't know. A client treats a status it doesn't know as settings it can't change, and shows the `problem` when one comes.

engineSettingsOk.description: The engine read its stored settings (or had none), and they can be changed: no `problem`.

version.description: How many changes this run of the engine made to the stored settings: 0 when it starts, one more after each change that changed them. A value equal to its default is stored, and `null` removes one, so either counts though the value in effect stays the same; a change that leaves the stored settings as they were (the value a setting already has, `null` for one that isn't set, `{}`) doesn't count. It counts within the run the session's and hello's `instance` name, and starts again at 0 when the engine restarts.

frameRate.description: Frames a second for every output without a rate of its own: 1 to 60, 15 by default. The preview socket keeps its own (subscribeMessage's `maxFps`).

graphRate.description: Milliseconds between the samples of the sensor history: 100 to 3000, 1000 by default.

clients.description: Each client's own preferences, by client name, as the client set them: the engine keeps them and never interprets them (docs/api.md#client-preferences). Empty when no client keeps any.

additionalProperties.description: A client's preferences: any JSON value but null.

engineSettingsProblem.description: The engine couldn't read its stored settings when it started: the defaults are in effect, `problem` says why, and every change is refused (409 settingsStatusProblem) until the stored settings are fixed or removed and the engine restarts.

status.description: `unreadable`: the engine couldn't read its stored settings; `unsupported`: they are another major version's. A client treats a status it doesn't know as settings it can't change.

problem.description: Why the engine couldn't read its stored settings, with a JSON pointer into them.

version.description: How many changes this run of the engine made to the stored settings: 0 when it starts, one more after each change that changed them. A value equal to its default is stored, and `null` removes one, so either counts though the value in effect stays the same; a change that leaves the stored settings as they were (the value a setting already has, `null` for one that isn't set, `{}`) doesn't count. It counts within the run the session's and hello's `instance` name, and starts again at 0 when the engine restarts.

frameRate.description: Frames a second for every output without a rate of its own: 1 to 60, 15 by default. The preview socket keeps its own (subscribeMessage's `maxFps`).

graphRate.description: Milliseconds between the samples of the sensor history: 100 to 3000, 1000 by default.

clients.description: Each client's own preferences, by client name, as the client set them: the engine keeps them and never interprets them (docs/api.md#client-preferences). Empty when no client keeps any.

additionalProperties.description: A client's preferences: any JSON value but null.

settingsSources.description: The settings of the engine's sensor sources, by source.

libreSettings.description: The settings of the LibreHardwareMonitor sensor source (on Windows): whether it reads sensors, whether it reads storage drives, and how often. An engine keeps them whether or not it has the source.

enabled.description: Whether the source reads sensors; true by default.

storage.description: Whether it reads storage drives' sensors; true by default.

storageInterval.description: Seconds between its reads of storage drives: 1 to 300, 30 by default.

mediaSettings.description: The settings of the engine's media providers (docs/providers.md).

localNetwork.description: Whether a provider may connect to this computer and the local network (docs/providers.md#addresses); true by default.

logLevel.description: How much the engine logs: the least severe entries it writes to its log, from `debug` (everything) through `information` and `warning` to `error` (errors only). A client shows a level it doesn't know by its name.

clientName.description: A client's name for its preferences (engineSettings' `clients`): 1 to 64 letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens. A client picks a name of its own, such as its product's name in lower case.

settingsChange.description: PATCH /api/settings: the settings to change (docs/api.md#changing-settings). A member given sets that setting, `null` sets it back to its default, and a setting left out keeps its value; `sources`, `sources.libre`, `media` and `clients` are merged member by member, each client's preferences set or removed whole. Closed: a member the engine doesn't know is refused. At most `settingsRequestBytes` as received, and the settings it makes are held to the settings limits (docs/limits.md#settings-limits).

clients.description: Client preferences to set, each whole, or to remove (`null`), by client name; the other clients' are kept.

additionalProperties.description: A client's preferences: any JSON value, or null to remove them.

settingsStatusProblem.description: 409 application/problem+json to PATCH /api/settings: the engine couldn't read its stored settings when it started (`unreadable`), or they are another major version's (`unsupported`), so it changes none of them until they are fixed or removed and the engine restarts. Nothing was changed.

code.description: The settings' status (engineSettings). A client treats a status it doesn't know as settings it can't change.

logPage.description: GET /api/logs: the engine's recent log entries newer than the request's `after`, oldest first, and the `seq` of the newest entry it has logged (docs/api.md#logs). A client polls with `after` set to the `latest` it last read. Read tolerantly: a client ignores members it doesn't know.

entries.description: The kept entries whose `seq` is greater than `after` (every kept entry without it), oldest first: at most the newest 2,000 of the run. When the first one's `seq` isn't `after` + 1, the engine dropped the entries between.

latest.description: The `seq` of the newest entry this run of the engine has logged, kept or not; 0 before the first. It belongs to the run the session's and hello's `instance` name.

logEntry.description: One of the engine's recent log entries, as its log file has it (docs/api.md#logs). `source`, `message` and `exception` are text for people, never a contract: a client shows them and never parses them.

seq.description: The entry's number: 1 for the run's first entry, one more for each entry after it, within the run the session's and hello's `instance` name.

time.description: When it was logged: RFC 3339 with milliseconds and the engine's offset from UTC, such as "2026-10-30T09:30:00.125+08:00".

level.description: How severe it is, from `verbose` through `debug`, `information` and `warning` to `error` and `fatal`. A client treats a level it doesn't know as `information`.

source.description: The part of the engine that logged it, for people, or empty; one longer than 256 characters is cut, ending in "…".

message.description: What it says, for people; one longer than 4,096 characters is cut, ending in "…".

exception.description: The error it records, as text for people, when there is one; one longer than 8,192 characters is cut, ending in "…".

displayList.description: GET /api/displays: the displays of the computer the engine runs on, read when the request came (docs/api.md#displays). Read tolerantly: a client ignores members it doesn't know.

supported.description: Whether this engine shows desktop windows, and so can list the displays. When false, `displays` is empty: a client tells "no displays" (true, and empty) from "this engine can't list them".

displays.description: The displays, the primary one first, then in the order the system gives them.

displayInfo.description: One display (docs/api.md#displays). `name`, `width`, `height`, `x` and `y` are exactly the `displayMatch` a profile's `window.display` takes to put its window on this display (urn:infopanel:document:1#/$defs/displayMatch).

name.description: The name the engine matches the display by, at most 256 characters (a longer one is cut).

width.description: The display's width in its own pixels.

height.description: The display's height in its own pixels.

x.description: The display's left edge in the desktop's own coordinates (points on macOS, not pixels on a scaled display).

y.description: The display's top edge in the desktop's own coordinates (points on macOS, not pixels on a scaled display).

label.description: The display's name for people, at most 256 characters (a longer one is cut): the same as `name` where the system has one name for it, else the name the system shows people.

scale.description: The display's pixels per unit of the desktop's own coordinates (2 on a Retina display on macOS).

primary.description: Whether it is the primary display (the main one, where a window without `display` goes). Only the first display listed is.

clientMessage.description: A text message a client sends on /ws (docs/api.md#the-preview-socket): a JSON object of at most 4,096 bytes in UTF-8, with a `type`. `auth` is only the first message, when the token wasn't offered as a subprotocol. Closed, as request bodies are (docs/versioning.md#unknown-members-and-values): the engine refuses a message with a member its definition doesn't have, as any other message it can't act on, with an error message (an `auth` message: by closing the socket).

authMessage.description: The first message on /ws when no `auth.{token}` subprotocol was offered: the token, within 5 seconds of the upgrade. The engine sends nothing before it; a token it doesn't accept, any other message, or none in time closes the socket with 1008.

token.description: The session token or an integration token (either has the `read` scope).

subscribeMessage.description: Subscribes to a profile's document: its doc messages and its frames, at `scale` and at most `maxFps` frames a second. It ends the connection's earlier subscription. A profile that doesn't exist or can't be opened is answered with an error message.

encoding.description: How the subscription's frames are encoded: `png` (the default), each frame a PNG; or `h264`, an H.264 video stream, with PNG frames that say why (`fallback`) where the engine can't send video (docs/api.md#video-frames). To change it, a client subscribes again.

viewMessage.description: Changes the current subscription's scale or frame rate; a member left out keeps its value. Without a subscription it is answered with an error message.

keyframeMessage.description: The client lost its video decoder's state: the engine's next `h264` frame of the current subscription is a keyframe, drawn at once if nothing changes. Nothing for a `png` subscription. Without a subscription it is answered with an error message.

unsubscribeMessage.description: Ends the subscription: no more doc messages or frames until the next subscribe.

frameRequestScale.description: The frame's pixels per profile pixel asked for, before the engine rounds and limits it (docs/api.md#frame-size). 1 when a subscribe leaves it out.

frameRequestFps.description: The most frames a second the client wants. 30 when a subscribe leaves it out; the engine draws at most 60.

serverMessage.description: A text message the engine sends on /ws (docs/api.md#the-preview-socket): a JSON object with a `type`. Frames are binary messages (frameHeader). Read tolerantly (docs/versioning.md#unknown-members-and-values): a client ignores a type and members it doesn't know.

helloMessage.description: The engine's first message on /ws, once the connection is authenticated.

protocol.description: The engine API's version, as GET /api/session gives it.

instance.description: This run of the engine, as GET /api/session gives it: another than the client saw before means the engine restarted.

profilesMessage.description: The profile list changed: a profile was created, duplicated or deleted, by any client. The client reads GET /api/profiles. The engine keeps only the newest to send.

version.description: How many times the list has changed in this run of the engine: greater for a later change.

settingsMessage.description: The engine settings changed: a change that changed the stored settings, by any client (PATCH /api/settings). Sent to every socket authenticated with the session token, the only token that reads the settings. The client reads GET /api/settings. The engine keeps only the newest to send.

version.description: The settings' `version` after the change (engineSettings): greater for a later change, within the run hello names.

errorMessage.description: Something the engine couldn't do for the client: a message it can't act on (not JSON, binary, an unknown type, a member the message doesn't define or of the wrong type, a view without a subscription), or a subscription to a profile that doesn't exist, can't be opened or previewed, or was deleted. The connection stays open.

code.description: What went wrong, for a client to act on (docs/api.md#errors-on-the-socket): `json`, `limit.jsonDepth` or `schema` for a message the engine can't act on, `subscription.missing` for a view without a subscription, `profile.*` for a subscription that didn't start or has ended. A later engine may add codes: a client handles a code it doesn't know by its family, else as a message the engine didn't act on (docs/versioning.md#error-codes-and-paths).

path.description: The JSON pointer to what the error is about in the client message it answers: "" for the whole message, or when it answers none (a subscription that ended).

message.description: What went wrong, for people: display text, never read by a client.

v1Migration.description: GET and PUT /api/import/v1: the 1.x migration (docs/import.md#migrating-a-1x-folder): its state, the 1.x folder the engine reads, the run-once record once there is one, and the folder's profiles, settings and diagnostics when it has 1.x data. Read tolerantly: a client ignores members it doesn't know.

state.description: `none` (the folder has no 1.x data), `pending` (1.x data and no record: not migrated yet) or `done` (a record, or one the engine can't read: the migration never runs on its own twice). A client treats a state it doesn't know as `done`: it doesn't migrate on its own.

folder.description: The 1.x folder the engine reads, as a full path. The engine only reads it.

record.description: The run-once record, when there is one the engine can read.

profiles.description: The folder's profiles, in 1.x order, when it has 1.x data (at most `v1Profiles`, docs/limits.md#1x-import-limits).

settings.description: The folder's settings, when it has 1.x data whose settings can be read (and isn't 1.1.x data).

diagnostics.description: What was found reading the folder and the record (docs/import.md#diagnostics): at most `diagnostics`, then one `more`.

v1MigrationRequest.description: PUT /api/import/v1: what a migration did, as a client reports it; the engine stores it as the run-once record (docs/import.md#the-record), adding the time and the folder. At most `recordOutcomes` outcomes, and at most `recordBytes` as received and as stored (docs/limits.md#1x-import-limits).

profiles.description: One outcome per 1.x profile the migration dealt with, in any order.

settings.description: Whether the client applied the 1.x settings (`imported`) or not (`skipped`). A client reading it treats a value it doesn't know as `skipped`.

v1MigrationRecord.description: The run-once record: what a migration did, as a client reported it, with when the engine stored it and the 1.x folder it read.

completed.description: When the engine stored the record, in UTC to the second.

folder.description: The 1.x folder the engine read then, as a full path.

settings.description: Whether the client applied the 1.x settings (`imported`) or not (`skipped`). A client treats a value it doesn't know as `skipped`.

v1MigrationOutcome.description: What a migration did with one 1.x profile.

v1Id.description: The 1.x profile's Guid, in lower case.

id.description: The profile created from it, or null when none was.

outcome.description: `imported`, `skipped` (the user left it out) or `failed`. A client treats an outcome it doesn't know as `failed`.

v1ProfileSummary.description: A profile of the 1.x folder's profile list, as 1.x lists it.

id.description: The 1.x profile's Guid, in lower case: what POST /api/import/v1/profiles/{v1Id} names.

name.description: Its name as stored (empty when it has none).

width.description: Its canvas width as stored, which may be over a document's limit (a client clamps it).

active.description: Whether 1.x showed it as a window.

v1Settings.description: The user data of the 1.x folder's settings (`settings.xml`, else `settings.xml.bak`), each value as 1.x would use it: an absent one is 1.x's default. Nothing is applied by reading it (docs/import.md#settings).

version.description: The settings version: 131 from 1.3.1 on, 115 from 1.2.x. Absent when it doesn't parse.

targetFrameRate.description: Frames a second, 1.x's default 15, within the engine setting's range.

targetGraphUpdateRate.description: Graph samples' interval in milliseconds, 1.x's default 1000, within the engine setting's range.

devices.description: The panel devices of 1.x's device families, at most `v1Devices` per family.

multiDevice.description: Per device family (as `v1Device.family` names it), whether 1.x drove several devices of it.

v1LibreSettings.description: 1.x's LibreHardwareMonitor settings: whether it read sensors with it, and whether and how often it kept their readings.

storageInterval.description: Seconds, within the engine setting's range.

v1ProgramSpecificSettings.description: Whether 1.x switched profiles by the program in front at all (its profiles' trigger apps), and whether it hid the other profiles then.

v1Device.description: A panel device of one of 1.x's device families: the 1.x profile it showed, and every simple element of the device as stored, as strings, at most `v1DeviceFields`.

family.description: `beada`, `turing`, `lianLi`, `thermalright`, `thermaltake`, `jl`, `jonsbo` or `vmax`. A client leaves out a device of a family it doesn't know.

profile.description: The 1.x profile it showed, its Guid in lower case; absent for none.

fields.description: The device's elements by their 1.x names, each value as stored (at most `v1SettingLength` characters).

v1Hotkey.description: A 1.x hotkey as stored: the keys, the device it targets and the 1.x profile it switches to.

profile.description: The 1.x profile it switches to, its Guid in lower case; absent for none.

v1Profile.description: POST /api/import/v1/profiles/{v1Id} and POST /api/import/v1/archive: one 1.x profile, read without installing anything (the envelope, docs/import.md#the-envelope): its properties, its items as the 1.x item JSON, its guides, its image files stored as blobs, and what was found on the way. A client creates a profile from it with POST /api/profiles, choosing the profile's id. Read tolerantly: a client ignores members it doesn't know.

source.description: `folder` (a profile of the 1.x folder) or `archive` (a 1.x `.infopanel` file). A client treats a source it doesn't know as `archive`.

id.description: The 1.x profile's Guid as stored, in lower case. It isn't a profile id of this engine: a client that creates a profile from the envelope chooses that.

items.description: The top-level items, in 1.x order, the first at the back (docs/import.md#items).

guides.description: 1.x's guides, wherever they sat among the items.

assets.description: One entry per image file the items name (gauge frames included), keyed by the items' `filePath` and `relativePath`.

diagnostics.description: What was found reading the profile (docs/import.md#diagnostics): at most `diagnostics`, then one `more`.

v1ProfileProps.description: Every member of the 1.x profile model, by its camelCase name, as stored. A string 1.x left null, or a number that isn't finite, is null.

width.description: As stored, which may be over a document's limit (a client clamps it, `import.size`).

active.description: Whether 1.x showed it as a window. A 1.x export writes the model's default, true.

font.description: The profile's default font family (`import.font` when the engine doesn't have it).

triggerProcessNames.description: The programs whose window in front shows the profile, as 1.x stored them (comma-separated).

v1TargetWindow.description: The display 1.x placed the profile's window on.

deviceName.description: The display's device name on Windows, such as "\\.\DISPLAY2".

v1ItemMeta.description: What the engine adds to a 1.x item: its sensor binding as this engine reads it now, and what the item's XML holds beyond the 1.x model the engine keeps (docs/import.md#the-envelope).

refreshInterval.description: An image item's RefreshInterval as stored, in seconds (0: never): how often a 1.x build that has it fetched the item's web image again. Absent when the item has none.

v1SensorMeta.description: The sensor a 1.x item is bound to: its key in this engine and its status now (`import.sensor` when it has no reading).

key.description: The sensor's key, as a binding names it (docs/bindings.md).

status.description: As `sensorEntry.status`: `live`, `stale`, `unavailable`, `denied`, `simulated` or `missing`. A client treats a status it doesn't know as no reading.

v1Guide.description: A 1.x guide (a line 1.x showed only while a profile was being designed, never on a panel): data for a client, not an item. A member 1.x left out has 1.x's default.

hidden.description: As stored: a guide in a hidden group keeps its own value (`container` tells the group).

container.description: The JSON pointer of the group's `children` the guide sat in (`/items/1/children`), in the answer's items; absent at the top level.

v1Asset.description: An image file the items name: the blob it was stored as, or why nothing was stored (docs/import.md#assets).

relative.description: Exactly the items' `relativePath`: the path is inside the profile's assets.

blob.description: The stored blob, as POST /api/blobs answers it.

code.description: Why nothing was stored: an `import.asset.*` code (docs/import.md#diagnostics). A later engine may add codes: a client treats one it doesn't know as a file that wasn't stored.

reason.description: With `import.asset.media`: the media check's code or the limit's (`media.format`, `limit.mediaBytes`, `limit.videoBytes`, `archive.expanded`, ...).

importDiagnostic.description: A problem found reading 1.x data, inside an otherwise readable answer (docs/import.md#diagnostics).

severity.description: `error` (something wasn't read), `warning` (read, but not as 1.x had it) or `info`. A client treats a severity it doesn't know as `warning`.

code.description: A code of docs/import.md's catalogue (`import.*`), or `more`, which counts the diagnostics not listed. A later engine may add codes: a client handles a code it doesn't know by its severity (docs/versioning.md#error-codes-and-paths).

path.description: The JSON pointer to what it is about, in the answer; "" for the whole.

message.description: What was found, for people: display text, never read by a client.

file.description: The 1.x file it was found in, as the folder or the archive names it (`profiles/{guid}.xml`, `Profile.xml`), when known.

line.description: The line in `file`, from 1, when known.

archiveContents.description: POST /api/import/archive: a profile archive opened and verified (docs/archive.md#importing): its document, to create a profile from with POST /api/profiles, the blobs it carried, each stored, and the blobs the document refers to that are neither in the archive nor stored here. Nothing else is stored or created. Read tolerantly: a client ignores members it doesn't know.

document.description: The archive's document, as it holds it: the shape a create takes.

blobs.description: Each blob the archive carried, stored, as POST /api/blobs answers it, in the archive's order.

missing.description: Blob ids the document refers to that the archive didn't carry and this engine doesn't store, in order: media naming one draws the missing-media placeholder until it is stored.

exportProblem.description: 409 application/problem+json to GET /api/profiles/{id}/archive: the profile's archive would be one its own import refuses, so it isn't made (docs/archive.md#exporting). Its errors carry the codes the import would give (`archive.entries`, `archive.expanded`), at "".
